title: Gen Z and Millennials Choose Different Travel Spots
paragraphs: Young travelers love to explore the world, but do Gen Z and millennials like the same places? According to a new study, the two generations often choose different destinations.

The study was done by Adventure360, a travel company for young people. It looked at more than 4,700 bookings made in the past year and found which countries were the most popular with each generation. The results were reported in August 2026.

For Gen Z, Thailand was by far the most popular country. In fact, 29.2% of Gen Z bookings included a visit to Thailand, the highest number for either generation. Next came Australia, Indonesia and Vietnam. Cambodia, Laos, Peru, the Philippines, New Zealand and Morocco completed the top 10.
For millennials, Australia was first, with 17.8%, and Thailand was a close second, with 17.4%. The Philippines, Japan, Indonesia, Peru, Morocco, Greece, Iceland and Vietnam completed the list.

Why are the lists different? One big reason is money. Japan, Greece and Iceland were on the millennials' list, but not on the Gen Z list, because these countries are more expensive. Jane McLellan-Green of Adventure360 said that a "£5 coffee in Reykjavík is a hard sell for Gen Z." In Laos, she said, the same money can pay for a bed for a night.

Cambodia, Laos and New Zealand were only on the Gen Z list. Cambodia and Laos are cheap, and they are popular on social media. New Zealand offers working holiday visas for many young people aged 18 to 35, but many millennials are now too old to get one.

Other research also shows that many young travelers want to avoid crowds. According to data from Skyscanner, 76% of Gen Z travelers are open to visiting a lesser-known place. And one in three say that crowds have spoiled a vacation in the past.
